post.caption: Trembler brooches shake diamonds on tiny springs. En tremblant is French for trembling. The flower sits on a tiny spring and quivers with every move. The shaking made diamonds flash in flickering candlelight. The style was popular in the 1700s and 1800s. The idea is older, with trembler pins worn in the 1600s. A diamond flower spray from about 1850 sparkles more on springs. Worn on a bodice, its flowers could also go in the hair. Insect brooches put wings on springs, so they seemed to move. Pforzheim, Germany, has a trembler flower bouquet with diamonds and emeralds.
